hook.line: The assembly will not happen on the date everyone hoped for, and somebody chose that. Spanish has two verbs for a delay somebody decided, and other words for one that just happens.
hook.es: Pospusimos la reunión para el lunes.
hook.en: We postponed the meeting until Monday.

examples.es: La asamblea se aplazó hasta nuevo aviso.
examples.en: The assembly was postponed until further notice.

examples.es: Pospusimos la reunión para el lunes.
examples.en: We postponed the meeting until Monday.

examples.es: La junta decidió posponer la votación.
examples.en: The board decided to postpone the vote.

examples.es: Aplazaron la asamblea para el sábado.
examples.en: They postponed the assembly until Saturday.

examples.es: El vuelo tuvo una demora de dos horas.
examples.en: The flight had a two-hour delay.

examples.es: El bus llegó con un retraso de veinte minutos.
examples.en: The bus arrived with a twenty-minute delay.

rule:
*Aplazar* and *posponer* mean someone decided to move it to later. The new date follows *para* or *hasta*: *para el lunes*, *hasta nuevo aviso* (until further notice).

*Posponer* is built on *poner*, so it is irregular: *pospuse*, *pospusimos*. With no one named, use *se*: *se aplazó*.

When nobody chose the delay, Spanish does not use these verbs. It says *una demora* or *un retraso de dos horas*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *se aplazó* the passive *se*: the thing is postponed and nobody is named.

readAndPick.es: Pospusimos la reunión para el lunes.
options: We brought the meeting forward to Monday.
We held the meeting on Monday.
We postponed the meeting until Monday.

readAndPick.es: La asamblea se aplazó hasta nuevo aviso.
options: The assembly was cancelled for good.
The assembly was postponed until further notice.
The assembly was held without notice.

readAndPick.es: El vuelo tuvo una demora de dos horas.
options: The flight had a two-hour delay.
The flight was cancelled two hours ago.
The flight lasts two hours.

readAndPick.es: La junta decidió posponer la votación.
options: The board decided to hold the vote.
The board decided to cancel the vote.
The board decided to postpone the vote.

readAndPick.es: Aplazaron la asamblea para el sábado.
options: They held the assembly on Saturday.
They postponed the assembly until Saturday.
They brought the assembly forward to Saturday.

options: The bus arrived twenty minutes late.
The bus arrived twenty minutes early.
The bus waited twenty minutes.
We had to make the payment.
We had to cancel the payment.
We had to postpone the payment.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *para* or *por*: Pospusimos la reunión ___ el lunes. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Pospusimos la reunión para el lunes.
accept: Aplazamos la reunión para el lunes.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The assembly was postponed until further notice.
yourTurn.answer: La asamblea se aplazó hasta nuevo aviso.
accept: La asamblea se pospuso hasta nuevo aviso.
yourTurn.why: *Se aplazó* leaves out who decided, and *hasta nuevo aviso* is the fixed phrase.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: We postponed the meeting until Monday.
yourTurn.answer: Pospusimos la reunión para el lunes.
accept: Aplazamos la reunión para el lunes.
yourTurn.why: Either verb works, and *para* introduces the new date.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The board decided to postpone the vote.
yourTurn.answer: La junta decidió posponer la votación.
accept: La junta decidió aplazar la votación.
yourTurn.why: After *decidió*, the verb stays in the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The flight had a two-hour delay. (nobody chose it)
yourTurn.answer: El vuelo tuvo una demora de dos horas.
accept: El vuelo tuvo un retraso de dos horas.
yourTurn.why: Nobody chose it, so Spanish uses *demora* or *retraso*, not *aplazar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about *they*: *Pospusimos la reunión para el lunes.*
yourTurn.answer: Pospusieron la reunión para el lunes.
accept: Aplazaron la reunión para el lunes.
yourTurn.why: *They* in the past ends in *-ieron* for *posponer*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about *I*: *Tuvimos que aplazar el pago.*
yourTurn.why: *Tuve* is the *I* form of *tener* in the past.

pitfalls.wrong: El vuelo tuvo un aplazamiento de dos horas.
pitfalls.right: El vuelo tuvo una demora de dos horas.
pitfalls.why: A delay nobody chose is a *demora* or *retraso*. *Aplazar* is for decisions.

pitfalls.wrong: Pospuse la reunión en el lunes.
pitfalls.right: Pospuse la reunión para el lunes.

pitfalls.wrong: Posponí la reunión para el lunes.
pitfalls.right: Pospuse la reunión para el lunes.

personal: Say something you would like to put off: *Quiero posponer…* or *Voy a aplazar…*, and when it moves to with *para*.
